content.text:
I made three small refactors, each its own commit with the reason in the message. The tests pass after each one, and clippy is clean.

The crate was already in good shape. It has typed errors, no stray `unwrap` on input, and tidy module boundaries. So I limited the changes to places where one fact was written down twice.

- **`d77d85c`**: The visibility-timeout limit (43,200) and delay limit (900) were bare literals in the attribute parser and the message commands. They are now named constants.
- **`a1d0747`**: `CreateQueue` and `SetQueueAttributes` each had a copy of the rule that content-based deduplication needs a FIFO queue. It is now one method on `AttributeUpdate`.
- **`00d71f4`**: In `Queue::expire`, the expiry closure was built before the early return that usually exits. I moved it below the return.

I left some things alone on purpose:

- **Repeated parameter reads:** Many handlers repeat `params.require(...)` followed by `string(...).expect("required")`. A helper for that would risk changing the order in which errors are checked, so I didn't touch it.
- **`as usize` cast:** The `max_messages as usize` cast in `receive_message` is bounded to 1–10, so it is safe.

I made three small refactors, each its own commit with the reason in the message. The tests pass after each one, and clippy is clean.

The crate was already in good shape. It has typed errors, no stray `unwrap` on input, and tidy module boundaries. So I limited the changes to places where one fact was written down twice.

- **`d77d85c`**: The visibility-timeout limit (43,200) and delay limit (900) were bare literals in the attribute parser and the message commands. They are now named constants.
- **`a1d0747`**: `CreateQueue` and `SetQueueAttributes` each had a copy of the rule that content-based deduplication needs a FIFO queue. It is now one method on `AttributeUpdate`.
- **`00d71f4`**: In `Queue::expire`, the expiry closure was built before the early return that usually exits. I moved it below the return.

I left some things alone on purpose:

- **Repeated parameter reads:** Many handlers repeat `params.require(...)` followed by `string(...).expect("required")`. A helper for that would risk changing the order in which errors are checked, so I didn't touch it.
- **`as usize` cast:** The `max_messages as usize` cast in `receive_message` is bounded to 1–10, so it is safe.
